disposition_reason: Reports iron, zinc, copper, lead, cadmium and tin in four canned tuna samples and iron, zinc, copper, lead and cadmium in four processed beef products from the Egyptian market.

period.as_reported: tuna produced Jan-May 2020, analysed March 2021; meat products produced May-June 2021, analysed June 2021

study.method: oven drying 105 °C, dry ashing 550 °C, HNO3 dissolution; flame AAS (Thermo S series), triplicates
study.qa: calibration standards only; no CRM, recovery or LOD reported

material.label_as_printed: Canned tuna (drained, in soybean oil and brine)

findings.notes: One can per production month, analysed in triplicate (SD is analytical). Analysed March 2021, 10-14 months after production.

controls.comparator: tuna cans produced in different months, analysed same date
controls.outcome: Pearson correlations: production date vs Cu r=0.99, Cd r=0.92, Fe r=0.69, Pb r=0.48, Zn r=0.36, Sn r=-0.29 (n=4)

unresolved: Basis of results not stated (samples were oven dried before ashing; results may be dry weight).
Each product type is a single sample; no between-sample variability.
No LOD/QA reported; lead and cadmium values (1-3.8 mg/kg) are high and analytical quality is uncertain.
Accepted date printed as 27 Feb 2021, before the 12 Jan 2022 received date (journal header typo).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Limits quoted by authors for canned fish Pb (CIFA 0.35, FAO/WHO 0.5, EC 0.2/0.3 mg/kg) and Cd (FAO/WHO 0.5, EC 0.1 mg/kg); Sn 250 mg/kg; Cu 3 mg/kg in meat products
